newsitem.title: UK: Moody's, S&P have no comment on Brazil rating talk.
newsitem.headline: Moody's, S&P have no comment on Brazil rating talk.

text.p: Major credit rating agencies Moody's Investors Service and Standard & Poor's had no comment on market rumours that Brazil's sovereign rating may be upgraded soon, officials at the agencies said on Wednesday.
Prices of Brazil Brady bonds strengthened amid the rumours on Wednesday, traders said.
An S&P official on the sovereign ratings desk in London declined to comment on the rumours.
But he said Brazil's rating outlook had been assigned positive last year, which signified that an upgrade was possible in the medium term.
A Moody's official declined immediate comment and referred questions to the agency's New York office.
IBCA, the European rating agency, said it had no plans in the short-term for changes in Brazil's ratings.
"Obviously, we keep things under review but at the moment we rate Brazil's long-term foreign currency at B plus," said an IBCA spokeswoman.
Brazil's long term foreign currency debt rating is B plus from S&P and B1 from Moody's.
